points.title: 王室公主
points.description: 1533年9月7日，伊丽莎白出生于伦敦格林尼治宫，是亨利八世和安妮·博林的女儿。她的出生引发了宗教和政治风波，因为亨利八世为了娶她的母亲而与罗马教廷决裂，创立英国国教。然而，在伊丽莎白三岁时，她的母亲被处决，她被降为私生女。这段早期经历塑造了她谨慎、独立的性格，也让她学会了在复杂的政治环境中保护自己。
points.descriptionEn: Born on September 7, 1533, at Greenwich Palace, Elizabeth was the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn. Her birth triggered religious and political turmoil as Henry had broken with Rome to marry her mother, establishing the Church of England. However, when Elizabeth was three, her mother was executed, and she was declared illegitimate. These early experiences shaped her cautious, independent character and taught her how to navigate the complex political landscape to protect herself.

points.placeEn: London and various locations in England
points.title: 教育时期
points.description: 在亨利八世去世后，伊丽莎白接受了当时欧洲最优质的教育之一。她精通拉丁语、法语、意大利语、希腊语等多种语言，还学习了数学、哲学、音乐、修辞学和古典文学。她的导师包括著名学者罗杰·阿斯坎和约翰·凯尔。这段教育经历为她后来的统治奠定了知识基础，使她成为文艺复兴时期最博学的君主之一。她展现出非凡的智力，能够与当时欧洲最杰出的学者交流，这为她日后处理复杂的政治和宗教事务提供了能力。
points.descriptionEn: After Henry VIII's death, Elizabeth received one of the finest educations in Europe at the time. She mastered multiple languages including Latin, French, Italian, and Greek, and studied mathematics, philosophy, music, rhetoric, and classical literature. Her tutors included renowned scholars Roger Ascham and John Cheke. This educational foundation prepared her for her future reign, making her one of the most learned monarchs of the Renaissance period. She demonstrated exceptional intellect, able to converse with the most prominent scholars of Europe, which equipped her to handle the complex political and religious affairs of her reign.

points.title: 危机岁月
points.description: 玛丽一世即位后，伊丽莎白作为新教徒继承人面临生命危险。1554年，她被卷入托马斯·怀亚特的叛乱，被囚禁于伦敦塔。尽管证据不足，玛丽仍将她关押数周，后转至伍斯特郡软禁。这段经历使伊丽莎白深刻认识到政治斗争的危险性，也锻炼了她在逆境中的应变能力。1558年玛丽去世后，伊丽莎白成为英格兰女王，结束了这段充满不确定性的时期。她在危机中展现出的冷静和智慧，为她未来的统治风格奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After Mary I's accession, Elizabeth faced danger as a Protestant heir. In 1554, she was implicated in Wyatt's rebellion and imprisoned in the Tower of London. Despite insufficient evidence, Mary confined her for weeks before moving her to house arrest in Worcestershire. This experience made Elizabeth acutely aware of the dangers of political struggle and honed her ability to navigate adversity. When Mary died in 1558, Elizabeth became Queen of England, ending this period of uncertainty. The composure and wisdom she displayed during these crises laid the foundation for her future ruling style.

points.title: 统治初期
points.description: 1558年11月17日，伊丽莎白在伦敦西敏宫加冕为英格兰女王。她面临的首要挑战是恢复宗教稳定，在天主教和新教之间寻找平衡。她通过《至尊法案》确立自己为英国国教最高领袖，同时采取相对宽容的宗教政策，避免了宗教迫大规模迫害。在外交方面，她与法国和西班牙保持谨慎关系，避免卷入欧洲大陆冲突。1569年，北方叛乱爆发，伊丽莎白果断镇压，巩固了王权。这一时期，她开始建立自己的统治团队，包括威廉·塞西尔等忠诚顾问，为长期统治奠定基础。
points.descriptionEn: On November 17, 1558, Elizabeth was crowned Queen of England at Westminster Palace. Her primary challenge was restoring religious stability, finding a balance between Catholicism and Protestantism. She established herself as Supreme Governor of the Church of England through the Act of Supremacy while maintaining relatively tolerant religious policies, avoiding large-scale religious persecution. Diplomatically, she maintained cautious relations with France and Spain, avoiding involvement in European continental conflicts. In 1569, the Northern Rebellion broke out, and Elizabeth decisively suppressed it, consolidating royal authority. During this period, she began building her ruling team, including loyal advisors like William Cecil, laying the foundation for her long reign.

points.placeEn: London and various locations in England
points.title: 黄金时代
points.description: 1570年代至1580年代是伊丽莎白统治的黄金时期。1570年，教皇将她开除教籍，反而强化了她的民族主义立场。1580年代，她支持英国海盗活动，如弗朗西斯·德雷克袭击西班牙船只，积累了财富并削弱了西班牙力量。1587年，她签署处决苏格兰女王玛丽·斯图亚特的命令，消除了潜在威胁。1588年，西班牙无敌舰队入侵英格兰，伊丽莎白激励军队，亲自视察军队，发表著名演说"我拥有弱小的身体，但我拥有国王的心"。这一时期，英国文学艺术繁荣，莎士比亚、斯宾塞等作家创作了大量作品，伊丽莎白时代成为英国文化史上的辉煌篇章。
points.descriptionEn: The 1570s to 1580s marked the golden age of Elizabeth's reign. In 1570, the Pope excommunicated her, which反而 strengthened her nationalist position. In the 1580s, she supported British privateering, such as Francis Drake's attacks on Spanish ships, accumulating wealth and weakening Spanish power. In 1587, she signed the warrant for the execution of Mary, Queen of Scots, eliminating a potential threat. In 1588, when the Spanish Armada invaded England, Elizabeth inspired her troops, personally inspected the army, and delivered her famous speech: "I have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a king." During this period, English literature and arts flourished, with writers like Shakespeare and Spenser creating numerous works, making the Elizabethan era a glorious chapter in British cultural history.

points.title: 晚年统治
points.description: 击败西班牙无敌舰队后，伊丽莎白进入统治晚期。尽管取得了军事胜利，但英国经济面临挑战，爱尔兰叛乱持续不断。伊丽莎白越来越依赖罗伯特·塞西尔等顾问，政治决策变得更加保守。她拒绝多次婚姻提议，保持"童贞女王"形象，但与罗伯特·德弗罗的关系引发争议。1601年，埃塞克斯伯爵叛乱被镇压，标志着她统治的转折点。随着年龄增长，伊丽莎白的健康状况恶化，1603年3月24日在里士满宫去世，享年69岁。她的统治结束了都铎王朝，开启了斯图亚特王朝，但她留下的稳定国家、繁荣文化和强大海军，为英国成为世界强国奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: After defeating the Spanish Armada, Elizabeth entered the later phase of her reign. Despite military victory, England faced economic challenges, and the Irish rebellion continued. Elizabeth increasingly relied on advisors like Robert Cecil, and her political decisions became more conservative. She rejected numerous marriage proposals, maintaining her image as the "Virgin Queen," though her relationship with Robert Devereux sparked controversy. In 1601, the Earl of Essex's rebellion was suppressed, marking a turning point in her reign. As she aged, Elizabeth's health deteriorated, and she died at Richmond Palace on March 24, 1603, at the age of 69. Her reign ended the Tudor dynasty and began the Stuart era, but the stable nation, flourishing culture, and powerful navy she left behind laid the foundation for Britain's emergence as a world power.

supporter.zh: 伊丽莎白一世被视为英国历史上最伟大的君主之一。她成功结束了宗教纷争，建立了稳定的英国国教；击败西班牙无敌舰队，维护了国家独立；支持文艺复兴，使英国文化空前繁荣。她的智慧、勇气和政治远见，使她在男性主导的欧洲政治舞台上脱颖而出。她终身未婚，将全部精力投入国家治理，展现出非凡的奉献精神。伊丽莎白时代成为英国历史上的黄金时代，她的统治为英国成为世界强国奠定了基础。
supporter.en: Elizabeth I is regarded as one of England's greatest monarchs. She successfully ended religious conflicts, established the stable Church of England; defeated the Spanish Armada, preserving national independence; and supported the Renaissance, making English culture flourish unprecedentedly. Her wisdom, courage, and political foresight allowed her to stand out in the male-dominated European political arena. She remained unmarried throughout her life, dedicating all her energy to state governance, demonstrating extraordinary commitment. The Elizabethan era became a golden age in British history, and her reign laid the foundation for Britain's emergence as a world power.

critic.zh: 批评者指出伊丽莎白统治的诸多局限性。她的宗教政策虽然相对宽容，但仍对天主教徒进行迫害；她对爱尔兰的镇压手段残酷，导致长期冲突；她支持海盗活动，虽然削弱了西班牙，但也损害了英国的国际声誉。伊丽莎白晚年变得固执多疑，如处决玛丽·斯图亚特和镇压埃塞克斯伯爵叛乱。她拒绝明确继承人，导致在她死后出现权力真空。此外，她对贫困问题关注不足，社会不平等现象严重。这些批评表明，尽管伊丽莎白取得了显著成就，但她的统治也存在明显的道德和政治缺陷。
critic.en: Critics point out several limitations of Elizabeth's reign. Although her religious policies were relatively tolerant, she still persecuted Catholics; her suppression of Ireland was brutal, leading to long-term conflicts; and her support for piracy, while weakening Spain, damaged Britain's international reputation. In her later years, Elizabeth became stubborn and suspicious, as evidenced by the execution of Mary, Queen of Scots, and the suppression of the Earl of Essex's rebellion. She failed to name a clear successor, creating a power vacuum after her death. Additionally, she paid insufficient attention to poverty issues, and social inequality was severe. These criticisms indicate that despite her significant achievements, Elizabeth's rule had notable moral and political flaws.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，伊丽莎白一世被复杂地定义和符号化。历史学者将她视为精明的政治家和宗教调和者，她的统治代表了英国民族意识的形成和国家主权的确立。流行文化则将她浪漫化为"童贞女王"，强调她的魅力、智慧和坚定的领导力。莎士比亚等作家的作品使她成为永恒的文化符号。现代历史研究强调她在性别政治中的独特地位，作为在男性主导的世界中成功的女性统治者。伊丽莎白既是历史人物，也是文化偶像，她的形象不断被重新诠释，反映了不同时代对权力、性别和民族身份的理解。
objective.en: In historical scholarship and popular culture, Elizabeth I is complexly defined and symbolized. Historians view her as a shrewd politician and religious reconciler, whose reign represented the formation of English national identity and the establishment of national sovereignty. Popular culture romanticizes her as the "Virgin Queen," emphasizing her charm, wisdom, and steadfast leadership. Works by writers like Shakespeare have made her an eternal cultural symbol. Modern historical research highlights her unique position in gender politics as a successful female ruler in a male-dominated world. Elizabeth is both a historical figure and a cultural icon, her image constantly reinterpreted to reflect different understandings of power, gender, and national identity across eras.

self.zh: 我拥有弱小的身体，但我拥有国王的心。
self.en: I have the body of a weak and feeble woman, but I have the heart and stomach of a king.

others.zh: 她统治的时期是英国历史上最辉煌的时代之一，她本人是那个时代最杰出的人物。
others.en: The period of her reign was one of the most glorious in English history, and she herself was the most remarkable figure of that era.
